physicalNotes: Radius 0.21866395 Jupiter radii from Eschen et al. 2025 (2025MNRAS.544.2614E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2614E/abstract): 15,632.7 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.02287398 Jupiter masses (Eschen et al. 2025, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2025MNRAS.544.2614E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2614E/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Eschen et al. 2025 (2025MNRAS.544.2614E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ESCHEN_ET_AL_2025): P 21.064302 d
sources.shape: Eschen et al. 2025 (2025MNRAS.544.2614E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ESCHEN_ET_AL_2025): a/R* 37.07; Eschen et al. 2025 (2025MNRAS.544.2614E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ESCHEN_ET_AL_2025): inclination 89.914 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Eschen et al. 2025 (2025MNRAS.544.2614E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ESCHEN_ET_AL_2025): transit mid-time 2459120.3007 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 6 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
